systems.title: Ingress
systems.subtitle: Authenticate & normalize
systems.description: Work enters through an authenticated API or a signed provider webhook. Provider-specific requests become an owner-scoped Run request.
facts: API identity determines the owner; a caller cannot supply an arbitrary owner ID.
GitHub, GitLab, Teams and Slack each have their own ingress adapter.

components.title: Control API
components.subtitle: API Gateway · Lambda
components.description: The control API exposes Runs, Things, connections, artifacts and thread continuity to clients and the reference console.
facts: Authenticated requests derive their owner from the principal.
Discovery and schemas describe the installed deployment.
components.inputs: An authenticated request, prompt and optional idempotency key.
components.outputs: HTTP 202 and an owner-scoped Run receipt; status and artifacts can be fetched later.
components.mechanics: The principal supplies ownership. Live event, steer and interrupt routes reach an active worker through the trusted control adapter.
components.failure: Invalid requests are rejected. A 202 response means accepted, not that execution or notification has finished.

components.title: Signed webhooks
components.subtitle: GitHub · GitLab · Teams · Slack
components.description: Each adapter verifies the provider signature before parsing and normalizing the request.
facts: Invalid signatures are rejected before submission.
The ingress service applies source policy and records trusted provenance.
components.inputs: A provider event body and its signature headers.
components.outputs: A normalized request with trusted source and identity context.
components.mechanics: The provider adapter verifies the signature before parsing; ingress applies source policy before submitting work.
components.failure: An invalid signature stops the request before a Run is submitted.

components.title: Identity context
components.subtitle: Actor ≠ owner ≠ credential subject
components.description: An actor starts work, an owner owns the Run, a source records origin, and a destination determines where the result goes.
facts: Credential subject is distinct from the actor and owner.
Provider payload details stay behind ingress and delivery adapters.
components.inputs: An authenticated principal or trusted provider identity mapping.
components.outputs: Separate actor, owner, source and credential-subject values.
components.mechanics: Ownership scopes the Run. Attribution records who initiated it; provider credentials remain deployment-owned.
components.failure: Missing identities are rejected. Being named as an actor does not grant provider credentials.

systems.inputs: A caller request or signed provider event.
systems.mechanics: API and webhook transports establish identity before passing work to coordination.
systems.failure: Invalid authentication, signatures or request policy stop submission.

systems.title: Coordination
systems.subtitle: Accept, persist & queue
systems.description: Every accepted execution has one durable Run receipt. The control layer records the request before sending a wake-up to execution.
facts: Things package reusable work as versioned definitions.
Threaded work uses a durable mailbox and a lease to coordinate turns.

sources.anchor: // One accepted input is one public Run.

components.title: Run service
components.subtitle: One accepted input · one Run
components.description: Submission validates the request, writes its input to S3 and conditionally creates a queued Run before enqueueing it.
facts: An idempotent retry reuses the same request and receipt.
A missed enqueue leaves a durable queued Run that can be recovered.
components.inputs: An owner, validated request and optional idempotency key.
components.outputs: One durable queued Run referencing its stored input, followed by a queue wake-up.
components.mechanics: Store the request in S3 before conditionally creating its record. A matching idempotent retry reuses the receipt and can re-send a queued wake-up.
components.failure: If enqueue fails, the queued record survives. Reusing a key with different request content is rejected.

components.title: Things & schedules
components.subtitle: Reusable, immutable revisions
components.description: Things carry versioned definitions for reusable work. Published revisions can be executed directly or triggered by a schedule.
facts: Draft, test and publish are distinct lifecycle operations.
The scheduler invokes the Thing schedule transport adapter.
components.inputs: An owner-scoped work definition with its agent, inputs and trigger.
components.outputs: Immutable revisions and Run receipts tied to the invoked revision.
components.mechanics: Editing advances the draft. Publishing requires a successful test of that exact draft before activating its trigger.
components.failure: A stale revision or mismatched test cannot be published. A schedule does not execute an inactive Thing.

components.title: Conversation mailbox
components.subtitle: DynamoDB lease · SQS wake-up
components.description: The coordinator acquires a conversation lease, prepares trusted continuation input and wakes the existing Run for the next turn.
facts: One accepted input remains one public Run, even when it waits for a predecessor.
Checkpoint and turn state let subsequent work continue a conversation.
components.inputs: A conversation message and its already reserved Run receipt.
components.outputs: Prepared execution input, predecessor context and a wake-up for that same Run.
components.mechanics: A lease orders turns. The coordinator keeps one accepted input per Run and carries durable context into a resumed or replacement worker.
components.failure: A busy lease delays work. An attach/enqueue crash can be repaired without combining several inputs into another Run.

components.title: Run queue
components.subtitle: Amazon SQS
components.description: The queue carries a Run reference and trace ID to the dispatcher. The request body remains in artifact storage.
facts: Dispatch claims are conditional; duplicate deliveries do not create a second independent Run.
Failed deliveries have a dead-letter queue.
components.inputs: A compact message containing version, Run ID and trace ID.
components.outputs: A delivery that asks the dispatcher to reload the durable Run.
components.mechanics: SQS is a wake-up mechanism. It does not hold the canonical prompt; conditional Run claims handle duplicate deliveries.
components.failure: A lost wake-up can be re-sent from durable state. Repeated queue delivery failures can reach the dead-letter queue.

systems.inputs: A normalized request or published Thing occurrence.
systems.outputs: Durable input and one queued Run; conversation work receives ordered context.
systems.mechanics: Persist before enqueueing. A Thing supplies reusable work; a conversation supplies continuity across distinct Runs.
systems.failure: Queue failure can leave recoverable durable work; an idempotency conflict rejects different content.

systems.title: Execution
systems.subtitle: An isolated agent runtime
systems.description: The dispatcher launches or resumes a Lambda MicroVM. Trusted orchestration prepares the workspace and runs Codex as a separate non-root process.
facts: The MicroVM is the outer isolation boundary.
The worker has no public user-facing ingress.

sources.anchor: Repairs stale attached Runs without ever replaying their semantic operation.

components.title: Run dispatcher
components.subtitle: Conditional claim · executor registry
components.description: The dispatcher reads stored input, claims the queued Run and starts its selected executor with a stable execution generation.
facts: A duplicate wake-up is safe after another dispatcher claims the Run.
An execution with the wrong generation is stopped.
components.inputs: A queue reference plus the Run and request loaded from storage.
components.outputs: An attached execution reference with a stable worker generation.
components.mechanics: Claim queued work conditionally, select the backend, then start and attach its execution. Threaded work waits until trusted input is prepared.
components.failure: Retryable start errors can be retried; permanent start errors fail the Run. A mismatched worker generation is stopped.

components.title: Lambda MicroVM
components.subtitle: ARM64 · launch or resume
components.description: The MicroVM adapter launches an isolated environment, or first tries to resume the preferred conversation MicroVM.
facts: An unavailable prior session can fall back to a new launch.
Conversation continuation goes through the service proxy with an AWS-issued token.
components.inputs: A Run reference, input location, execution generation and runtime configuration.
components.outputs: An isolated worker, optionally resumed from a conversation session.
components.mechanics: A preferred session is tried first. If unavailable, launch a replacement; lifecycle and live control use an AWS-issued port-scoped proxy token.
components.failure: An unavailable warm session can fall back to launch. Its memory is not the durable source of truth.

components.title: Codex runner
components.subtitle: Trusted host · non-root agent
components.description: The host prepares workspace files, credentials and allowed tools, starts the agent driver, then records results and artifacts.
facts: Agent processes use argument arrays and a separate UID.
Codex approval requests fail closed; they cannot widen the Run’s authority.
components.inputs: Stored execution input, resolved capabilities, workspace and trusted tool handlers.
components.outputs: Agent output, events and artifacts, then a fenced terminal Run update.
components.mechanics: Trusted host code starts Codex under a separate non-root UID. App Server exposes progress, steering and turn interruption within the admitted capability envelope.
components.failure: An approval-shaped request fails closed. Lost execution authority prevents the worker from committing an outcome.

components.title: Browser & tools
components.subtitle: Optional capability
components.description: When enabled for the Run, host-provided browser tools let the agent inspect and interact with a browser in the isolated environment.
facts: Browser actions are routed through the trusted tool handler.
Network and process policy are enforced by the runtime.
components.inputs: Allowed browser tool calls from the agent.
components.outputs: Browser observations and action results inside the worker.
components.mechanics: The trusted handler routes browser requests. Runtime network rules separate the non-root process from protected host ports.
components.failure: Unavailable tools and denied network access remain failures; a browser call cannot expand the Run’s authority.

components.title: Model access
components.subtitle: ChatGPT / OpenAI · Bedrock
components.description: The runner selects its Codex authentication mode. ChatGPT-backed access and explicit Amazon Bedrock configuration have separate host-side setup.
facts: Model authentication is prepared by trusted runner code.
Provider credentials do not belong in Run requests or repository URLs.
components.inputs: The selected model and deployment-owned authentication configuration.
components.outputs: Host-prepared model access used by Codex.
components.mechanics: ChatGPT-backed authentication and explicit Bedrock mode have separate setup. The selected provider is an external service, not a model hosted by this stack.
components.failure: Missing or invalid authentication blocks model access; provider tokens are not supplied in the Run request.

systems.inputs: A durable Run reference and its fixed capability envelope.
systems.outputs: Stored agent output and a terminal Run outcome.
systems.mechanics: Dispatch attaches a generation-scoped MicroVM. Trusted host orchestration starts the non-root agent and fences finalization.
systems.failure: A lost attached worker does not imply automatic re-execution; reconciliation records a fenced failure.

systems.title: Delivery
systems.subtitle: Persist, emit & notify
systems.description: Durable Run state drives completion events. A separate notifier resolves destinations and delivers the result behind a delivery fence.
facts: Completion is emitted from DynamoDB Streams after the state commit.
Terminal events also advance conversation completion.

components.title: State stream & events
components.subtitle: DynamoDB Streams → EventBridge
components.description: Run status changes are published from the table stream, closing the crash window between a state commit and a worker-side event.
facts: The stream handler retries unsuccessful event publishing.
Terminal Run events feed notification and conversation completion.
components.inputs: A committed insertion or status change in the Runs table.
components.outputs: A bounded state event with Run ID, owner, status and optional result preview.
components.mechanics: The stream handler publishes to EventBridge after the durable commit. Terminal events route separately to notification and conversation completion.
components.failure: A publish failure makes the stream handler fail for retry. Repeated events still pass through delivery fencing.

components.title: Result notifier
components.subtitle: Independent delivery stage
components.description: For a succeeded, failed or cancelled Run, the notifier loads stored input and results, resolves destinations and invokes the provider delivery adapter.
facts: Source-thread replies and configured destinations are resolved separately.
Retries do not require the agent to execute again.
components.inputs: A terminal Run event and its stored request and result.
components.outputs: A provider delivery attempt and destination-specific receipt or failure record.
components.mechanics: Resolve configured destinations or source replies, claim each destination fence, then send the stored result through its provider adapter.
components.failure: A succeeded Run can have an unsuccessful notification. Delivery handling reads the saved outcome without re-executing the agent.

components.title: Delivery fence
components.subtitle: Conditional destination claim
components.description: A DynamoDB fence coordinates each Run/destination delivery and records delivered or uncertain outcomes separately from execution.
facts: Duplicate terminal events are checked against the destination claim.
Only known retryable non-delivery releases the claim for retry.
components.inputs: A terminal Run and destination key.
components.outputs: A sending claim, delivered receipt, unknown outcome or released claim.
components.mechanics: DynamoDB conditionally claims each Run/destination. Only a known retryable non-delivery releases the claim for another attempt.
components.failure: An ambiguous send error is stored as outcome_unknown and is not blindly retried. The fence is not an exactly-once delivery guarantee.

components.title: Artifact publication
components.subtitle: Optional scoped sharing
components.description: Publication services turn selected artifacts into file, video or static-site publications using explicit publication grants.
facts: Publication builders validate and plan output before storage.
Sharing is a separate capability from completing a Run.
components.inputs: Selected owner-scoped artifacts and a publication specification.
components.outputs: A validated file, video or static-site publication with an explicit grant.
components.mechanics: Builders plan paths and content before storage. The publisher verifies artifact ownership and creates the sharing grant.
components.failure: Invalid paths, unknown source blobs or artifacts outside the owner’s scope are rejected before publication.

systems.outputs: A destination-specific delivery outcome or publication grant.
systems.mechanics: The notifier reads saved output and coordinates each send through a fence, independently of agent execution.
systems.failure: A successful Run can still have failed or uncertain delivery.

systems.title: Durable state
systems.subtitle: Receipts, files & checkpoints
systems.description: State and payloads have different homes: DynamoDB holds records and bounded summaries; encrypted S3 holds prompts, results and artifacts.
facts: Persistent conversations can mount Codex home and workspace through S3 Files.
Storage survives the lifetime of an individual worker.

components.title: DynamoDB records
components.subtitle: Runs · conversations · connections
components.description: DynamoDB stores durable Run state, identities, references and bounded summaries. Conditional writes enforce transitions and leases.
facts: Large prompts and results are stored by reference.
Things, routines and integrations have their own tables.
components.inputs: Run identity, input/output references and bounded lifecycle updates.
components.outputs: Durable receipts, state, execution identity and liveness evidence.
components.mechanics: Conditional writes enforce transitions and worker generations. Payloads remain in S3; the table stores their references.
components.failure: A stale worker or conflicting transition cannot overwrite the current Run state.

components.title: Encrypted artifacts
components.subtitle: Amazon S3 · KMS
components.description: Inputs, results and artifact payloads live in S3. Infrastructure configures encryption, public access blocking and retention.
facts: A Run record points to its stored input and output.
Thing definitions use a separate definitions bucket.
components.inputs: Input JSON, output text, execution events and artifact bytes.
components.outputs: Stored objects referenced by Run records and artifact catalogs.
components.mechanics: S3 holds the large payloads. The worker stores its output before committing the terminal record that points to it.
components.failure: A worker stopping does not erase already stored objects. An output write must succeed before successful finalization.

components.title: Persistent workspace
components.subtitle: Optional Amazon S3 Files
components.description: When S3 Files is enabled, conversation execution receives a filesystem and access point for durable native state and workspace files.
facts: The adapter includes S3 Files settings only for conversation executions.
A resumed agent can reuse its native thread and workspace.
components.inputs: Conversation storage settings and a native Codex thread identity, when enabled.
components.outputs: Workspace files and native agent state that can be reused across conversation workers.
components.mechanics: S3 Files is optional and applied only to conversation execution. Warm resume can reuse a session; a replacement can restore native state when persistent storage is configured.
components.failure: A warm worker can expire. Without S3 Files, durable Run records and conversation context remain, but native workspace persistence is not promised.

systems.inputs: Requests, state updates, results and conversation context.
systems.outputs: Durable records and references plus stored payloads.
systems.mechanics: DynamoDB holds state; S3 holds payloads. Optional S3 Files adds native conversation workspace persistence.
systems.failure: Worker memory may disappear while committed records and stored payloads remain.

systems.title: Access boundary
systems.subtitle: Fixed before launch
systems.description: A Run operates inside a fixed capability envelope. Profiles, requested narrowing, IAM, runtime policy and connection grants constrain what it can do.
facts: An operation outside the boundary is unavailable or denied.
There is no mid-Run approval path to expand authority.

components.title: Capability profiles
components.subtitle: Resolve & narrow
components.description: Trusted capability profiles determine the agent configuration. Run and Thing requests can narrow the admitted capabilities.
facts: The runtime resolves an agent profile before running the agent.
Tool availability is constrained by that resolved profile.
components.inputs: A trusted profile and optional Run or Thing restrictions.
components.outputs: An effective agent configuration and maximum integration access.
components.mechanics: Resolution takes the narrower sandbox, network, browser and tool settings. Requested selections must fit the installed profile.
components.failure: An unknown profile or disallowed selection is rejected. A request cannot use a profile to widen its configured limits.

components.title: Runtime & IAM policy
components.subtitle: Network · process · resources
components.description: IAM and runtime policies enforce the boundaries around the MicroVM, its network access and its agent process.
facts: The outer environment is the isolation boundary for danger-full-access.
Enforcement denies operations outside the configured envelope.
components.inputs: Deployment IAM permissions and runtime process and network settings.
components.outputs: Enforced permissions around the worker and the non-root agent process.
components.mechanics: The MicroVM provides the outer isolation boundary. Host rules protect credentials and lifecycle ports; IAM and grants constrain allowed operations.
components.failure: Operations beyond the boundary are denied. There is no mid-Run permission expansion or pending approval path.

components.title: Credential broker
components.subtitle: Host-side secret reader
components.description: The host reads and parses secret values through a credential broker. Requests identify allowed resources without carrying provider tokens.
facts: Secrets are held separately from Run metadata and task overrides.
OAuth-backed connections use a host-side vault and refresh broker.
components.inputs: A host-owned credential reference, after applicable authorization checks.
components.outputs: Parsed credential values supplied to trusted host-side callers.
components.mechanics: The broker reads a secret through its port and accepts structured or raw values. Integration tools check grants and resource constraints before reading credentials.
components.failure: A missing reference or unusable credential fails the call. Denied integration requests never reach the credential read.

systems.outputs: A fixed capability envelope enforced by several layers.
systems.mechanics: Profiles, IAM, process and network rules, provider scopes and connection grants determine what is available.
systems.failure: Out-of-envelope actions are denied; no mid-Run approval widens authority.

systems.title: Connected services
systems.subtitle: Granted operations & accounts
systems.description: Trusted integration manifests describe operations. The runtime exposes only tools that the selected accounts and their intersected grants allow.
facts: Tool authorization happens before credential access.
Slack, Linear and Stripe integrations are defined in this repository.

components.title: Trusted plugins
components.subtitle: Manifests & adapters
components.description: Provider plugins bind ingress and delivery capabilities. Integration plugins define separate operations for connected services.
facts: The registries validate trusted manifests.
Protocol parsing stays behind provider adapters.
components.inputs: Trusted provider or integration manifests and their implementations.
components.outputs: Validated provider capabilities and connected-service operation definitions.
components.mechanics: Provider registries bind ingress and delivery. The separate integration registry supplies operation metadata used to prepare granted tools.
components.failure: Invalid manifests are rejected. Installing a plugin alone does not grant an account or every operation.

components.title: Connection grants
components.subtitle: Account · operation · resource
components.description: The integration runtime intersects the stored connection grant with requested restrictions and maximum integration access.
facts: Disallowed operations are omitted from the agent’s tools.
Per-call resource checks run before credentials are read.
components.inputs: A selected active connection, stored grants and requested restrictions.
components.outputs: Only admitted operations, with per-call resource checks.
components.mechanics: Tool preparation intersects stored and requested access. Each call repeats operation authorization and checks resource fields before fetching a credential.
components.failure: Disallowed operations are absent or rejected. A valid account credential cannot bypass a denied resource constraint.

components.title: Connection lifecycle
components.subtitle: Install · refresh · health
components.description: Connection and OAuth services manage account installation and host-side credentials; a scheduled monitor checks connection health.
facts: Active connections and valid grants are required for tool preparation.
OAuth refresh is separate from guest execution.
components.inputs: Account installation state, OAuth credentials and connection health settings.
components.outputs: Stored connection metadata and host-managed refreshed credentials.
components.mechanics: Connection services manage account installation. The refresh broker works outside the guest, and a scheduled monitor checks connection health.
components.failure: An inactive connection is unavailable for tool preparation; credential refresh failures are separate from guest execution.

systems.inputs: Trusted plugins, active accounts and their access grants.
systems.outputs: A set of admitted tools and authorized connected-service calls.
systems.mechanics: Grants intersect before tool preparation; operation and resource checks run again before credential access.
systems.failure: An installed plugin or valid credential does not override a denied operation.

systems.title: Recovery
systems.subtitle: Reconcile & retry
systems.description: Recovery is built around durable state. Conditional transitions, execution heartbeats, reconciliation and dead-letter queues handle interruptions.
facts: The domain transition table defines legal Run state changes.
Duplicate deliveries and missing wake-ups are handled explicitly.

components.title: Run state machine
components.subtitle: Conditional transitions
components.description: The Run lifecycle admits only declared transitions. Succeeded, failed and cancelled are terminal states.
facts: A running Run can succeed, fail or enter cancellation.
Terminal states have no outgoing transitions.
components.inputs: The current Run status and a requested next status.
components.outputs: Permission to perform only a declared lifecycle transition.
components.mechanics: Queued work can be cancelled immediately. Owner cancellation of running work records cancelling before stopping it; succeeded, failed and cancelled are terminal.
components.failure: Invalid transitions throw. A terminal Run cannot transition back to running or be silently replayed.

components.title: Execution reconciler
components.subtitle: Repair stalled work
components.description: The reconciler inspects active execution and durable Run records to recover work after missed dispatch or worker failure.
facts: Recovery uses the same state and execution ports.
Provisioning tests remain an explicit opt-in operation.
components.inputs: Stale queued records or attached execution records with liveness evidence.
components.outputs: A repaired wake-up, verified liveness observation or fenced terminal update.
components.mechanics: Scheduled repair re-sends missing queued wake-ups. Attached workers are inspected against their backend ID, generation and heartbeat; their semantic work is not replayed.
components.failure: A confirmed lost execution is failed. Repeated unknown or conflicting inspections are quarantined instead of guessing or launching duplicate work.

components.title: Heartbeat & dead letters
components.subtitle: Liveness · failed deliveries
components.description: The runner reports execution liveness. Queue and event delivery failures have dedicated dead-letter queues and monitoring.
facts: Heartbeats identify the current execution generation.
Delivery failures remain separate from agent execution failures.
components.inputs: The active worker’s exact execution reference and current timestamp.
components.outputs: A generation-scoped heartbeat stored on the Run.
components.mechanics: A serial loop refreshes liveness. Reconciliation later compares that evidence with the actual execution before changing state.
components.failure: If the heartbeat loses authority, the runner aborts. A delayed heartbeat alone does not prove the worker has stopped.

systems.inputs: Durable state, worker generations and observed liveness.
systems.outputs: Repaired queued wake-ups or conditional lifecycle updates.
systems.mechanics: Repair separates work that never dispatched from work already attached to a worker.
systems.failure: Lost execution can fail; uncertain observations can be quarantined without replaying the operation.

connections.label: Protected live progress, steer and interrupt
Operation definitions checked against account access
Authorize operation and resources before credential read

steps.title: Authenticate the request
steps.description: The caller sends a prompt to the authenticated API. The principal determines the owner. This example requests a result destination for notification later.

steps.title: Accept one durable Run
steps.description: Store input in S3 and conditionally create a queued Run before enqueueing. The API returns HTTP 202 with its receipt now; acceptance does not mean the work is finished.

steps.description: SQS carries only the Run reference and trace ID. Its recipient reloads the canonical input from storage; duplicate wake-ups do not create a new receipt.

handoff.payload: Run ID + trace ID; prompt stays in S3

steps.title: Claim and launch

steps.title: Run inside the boundary

steps.title: Persist the outcome

steps.title: Coordinate the next turn

handoff.payload: Lease-ordered predecessor context + prepared execution input

steps.title: Find the waiting Run
steps.description: The scheduled reconciler queries stale queued records. It uses the durable record to choose the ordinary Run queue or conversation coordinator queue.

steps.title: Send another wake-up
steps.description: Re-send a reference to the same Run. An idempotent client retry can also repair this window; neither path regenerates the accepted request.

handoff.payload: Same Run ID; a new recovery wake-up

steps.title: Claim once from queued state
steps.description: The dispatcher conditionally claims the Run and starts its stable execution identity. Duplicate wake-ups race on that claim instead of creating independent Runs.

steps.title: Execute the accepted work
steps.description: This is the first execution of the waiting request. Recovery of an already attached, lost worker is different: it can mark failure and does not replay the semantic operation.

sources.anchor: Repairs stale attached Runs without ever replaying their semantic operation.

steps.title: Commit the recovered outcome
steps.description: Store the result and commit the terminal Run update. Recovery repaired delivery of the wake-up while preserving the original Run identity.

handoff.payload: Result and artifacts for the original Run

steps.title: Start with an active Run
steps.description: The Run is already running with an attached worker generation. Cancellation is a lifecycle request, distinct from steering an active Codex turn.

steps.title: Request cancellation
steps.description: The owner asks to cancel this Run. The service loads the owner-scoped record; an already terminal Run is returned unchanged.

steps.title: Record cancellation intent
steps.description: Running or dispatching work transitions to cancelling before the stop request. Queued work can instead become cancelled immediately.

steps.title: Ask the execution to stop
steps.description: The service stops the attached execution. The cancelling state records intent; it does not claim the worker is already gone.

steps.title: Verify a stale cancellation
steps.description: For a stale cancellation, inspect the exact execution. An active worker gets another stop request; unknown observations defer or quarantine instead of claiming it stopped.

steps.title: Finalize after confirmation
steps.description: When the inspected execution is terminal or absent, a fenced update can record cancelled. Terminal states have no outgoing transitions.

steps.title: Begin with saved output
steps.description: The agent finished and stored its result. The Run is succeeded; this scenario follows a later notification failure, not an execution failure.

handoff.payload: Committed result bytes and artifact references

steps.title: Route the terminal event
steps.description: A committed status change triggers notification. The event does not launch another agent execution.

steps.title: Claim this destination
steps.description: Before sending, the notifier claims the Run/destination fence. Already recorded outcomes are checked when duplicate terminal events arrive.

steps.title: Receive an ambiguous send error
steps.description: The provider call throws an error that does not prove safe non-delivery. The saved result remains available, and the Run stays succeeded.

steps.title: Keep the uncertain outcome
steps.description: Record outcome_unknown rather than blindly sending again. Only a known retryable non-delivery releases the claim and throws for a safe retry.

handoff.payload: Uncertain delivery outcome; retain the claim

steps.title: Retrieve the successful Run
steps.description: The owner can still retrieve the Run and its stored result through the API. Fixing or inspecting delivery does not require rerunning the agent.

concepts.title: Run
concepts.description: One accepted input creates one owner-scoped execution receipt. The Run records its lifecycle and points to stored input and output; acceptance happens before completion.

sources.anchor: // One accepted input is one public Run.

concepts.title: Thing
concepts.description: A versioned definition of reusable work. Testing a draft and invoking its published revision create Runs; a Thing is not a running worker.

concepts.title: Conversation
concepts.description: Ordering and continuity across inputs. A mailbox and lease prepare each Run with predecessor context; several inputs do not merge into one Run.

concepts.title: MicroVM
concepts.description: Replaceable execution capacity around the trusted host and non-root agent. A conversation may resume a warm session or start a replacement when it is unavailable.

concepts.title: What survives a worker
concepts.description: Committed Run records, conversation context and S3 payloads survive worker loss within configured retention. Optional S3 Files also preserves native conversation state and workspace files across workers.

concepts.title: Capability envelope
concepts.description: The Run starts with fixed authority. Profiles, IAM, network and process rules and connection grants enforce it; forbidden tools are absent or denied, with no mid-Run approval to widen access.

externals.title: Caller
externals.description: A person, application or provider outside the managed Run resources. Authenticated API calls and signed provider events enter through separate transports. The placement is logical, not a network topology.

externals.title: Result destination
externals.description: A source thread or configured provider destination receiving saved results. Delivery leaves the managed Run resources and has its own outcome; it does not loop back through ingress.

externals.title: Model provider
externals.description: The selected external model service, using ChatGPT-backed access or configured Amazon Bedrock. This is outside the worker’s process boundary; the drawing does not claim it is outside AWS.

externals.title: Connected service
externals.description: An external provider account reached through a trusted integration operation. Its own scopes and service rules still apply after Rat Things checks the connection grant. Placement denotes a logical service boundary.
